company: Scentre Group Limited (as responsible entity manager of Carindale Property Trust, ASX:CDP)
title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: All Employees
tiers.description: All Scentre Group Directors, officers and employees, whether or not classified as Restricted Persons. Bound at all times by the Insider Trading Prohibition; not subject to blackout periods, the section 5 clearance regime or section 11 (margin lending/short selling/short-term trading) unless also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Umbrella term (section 1) for Specified Persons, Designated Persons, and other employees likely to have access to market sensitive information in the ordinary course of employment. Subject to blackout periods, clearance to trade outside blackout periods, and the section 11 margin lending, short selling and short-term/speculative trading restrictions, which do not differentiate between the sub-tiers.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: A Scentre Group Director, any executive named as key management personnel in the Group's remuneration report, any Company Secretary, and any other person classified as a Specified Person by the Clearance Committee. Distinguished only for clearance: the Clearance Officer is the Clearance Committee (Chair of the Board and Chair of the Audit Committee).

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Members of the Executive Committee (other than Specified Persons), executive assistants and personal assistants of Specified Persons and Executive Committee members, executives and assistants within the legal/secretariat and compliance functions, and any other person notified as a Designated Person. Distinguished only for clearance: the Clearance Officer is the Chief Executive Officer.

tiers.name: Other Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Other Scentre Group employees prescribed as Restricted Persons who are neither Specified Persons nor Designated Persons. Distinguished only for clearance: the Clearance Officer is the Chief Financial Officer or Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associate
tiers.description: The immediate family of a Restricted Person (spouses, partners, children under 18), the trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement under which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary, and any entity (including family companies, family trusts and personal superannuation funds) over which the Restricted Person or their immediate family has or may be expected to have investment control or influence.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may extend a blackout period or specify any additional period as a blackout period. The Chief Executive Officer has discretion to impose ad hoc trading restrictions on employees directly involved in, or with knowledge of, matters withheld from disclosure under the Listing Rule 3.1A exception. The Policy does not state whether these are confidential.

rules.detail: An exchange-traded derivative over Scentre Group Securities (e.g. an ASX-quoted option) is 'able to be traded on a financial market' and so falls within the Scentre Group Securities definition, making it subject to the ordinary blackout and clearance regime in the same way as the underlying stapled securities or units.
rules.evidence: any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market

rules.detail: A bespoke, bilateral OTC derivative such as a bank-written put/call is not 'able to be traded on a financial market' and so falls outside the Scentre Group Securities definition, meaning the general blackout and clearance regime in sections 3-9 does not apply to entering it. It remains caught only by the free-standing short-term/speculative trading ban in 11(d) (which names 'Financial Products' without a market-tradability qualifier) and by the statutory Insider Trading Prohibition, which applies regardless of this policy's internal definitions.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements over unvested equity-linked incentive awards are prohibited; the substantive terms of the prohibition are set out in the separate Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy, which is not part of this document.
rules.evidence: Prohibitions also apply to executives entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards offered under the equity-linked incentive plans operated by Scentre Group. These prohibitions are outlined in the Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.

rules.detail: The hedging ban extends to awards that have vested but remain in a holding lock or are otherwise subject to deferral of delivery; again the substantive terms sit in the external Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.
rules.evidence: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery

rules.detail: Once an award is fully vested and released from any holding lock or deferral, the express hedging ban in 10(b) no longer applies; a hedge structured as an OTC derivative falls outside the Scentre Group Securities definition and so escapes the general blackout/clearance regime, subject only to the 3-month short-term/speculative ban and the Insider Trading Prohibition.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar arrangement is a 'forward contract', which is expressly a Financial Product; if bespoke and not market-tradable it sits outside the Scentre Group Securities definition and outside the general blackout/clearance regime, but is still caught by the 11(d) short-term/speculative ban and the statutory Insider Trading Prohibition.
rules.evidence: Financial Product means any financial instrument, including derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short selling Scentre Group Securities, with no stated clearance route.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short selling of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are expressly named within the Financial Product definition. As CFDs are typically bilateral OTC contracts not 'traded on a financial market', they sit outside the Scentre Group Securities definition and the general blackout/clearance regime, but remain caught by the 11(d) short-term/speculative ban and the Insider Trading Prohibition.
rules.evidence: Financial Product means any financial instrument, including derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on margin lending arrangements over Scentre Group Securities.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons may not enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest over Scentre Group Securities under a loan arrangement that is not properly described as a margin loan is expressly distinguished from the margin lending ban and is permitted subject to prior approval of the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: if a Restricted Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary prior to entering into any such arrangement

rules.detail: The prohibition in 11(a) is expressly confined to arrangements 'properly described as' margin lending; any other secured loan arrangement using Scentre Group Securities as security is permitted, subject to prior Company Secretary approval (and consultation if there is doubt about characterisation).
rules.evidence: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in any derivative or other Financial Product issued over or in respect of them; short-term is defined as less than 3 months. The section 9 excluded-trading list does not carve this ban out (it only excuses blackout-period trading under sections 3-4).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.

A Specified Person or Designated Person who receives clearance to trade in Scentre Group Securities must complete the trade within three business days of the clearance being received.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the trade occurring

clearance.approver: Chief Financial Officer or Company Secretary

exceptions.evidence: transfers of Scentre Group Securities that are already held by a Restricted Person into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

indirect or incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of an investment in, or trading in securities of a managed investment scheme ... that is managed by a third party ... where the assets of that vehicle are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Scentre Group Securities by that trust provided that the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during the blackout period is taken by the other trustee(s) or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person
undertakings to accept a takeover offer, or a disposal of Scentre Group Securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer or under a scheme of arrangement

participation in, acceptance of, or trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most Scentre Group (or Carindale Property Trust) security holders ... such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a distribution reinvestment plan (where there is a standing election) and an equal access buy-back

a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
the acquisition (but not the sale) of securities under the Group's Performance Rights Plan where the acquisition is during a blackout period

an acquisition or disposal of Scentre Group Securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... and the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade
transfers where the beneficial interest in the relevant Scentre Group Securities does not change (e.g. the transfer from one personal security holding to another)

A clearance to trade ("exceptional circumstances notice") may be given to a Restricted Person ... during a blackout period if he or she is in severe financial hardship, or is the subject of a court order or court enforceable undertaking or where there are other exceptional circumstances.

external_documents: Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy
Code of Conduct, Acting with Integrity
exemption_authority: A Clearance Officer may, in their absolute discretion and without giving reasons, issue an exceptional circumstances notice permitting the sale (not purchase) of Scentre Group Securities during a blackout period for severe financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, or other exceptional circumstances where the sale is the only reasonable course of action; Scentre Group may need to notify ASX of the nature of the circumstances. There is no equivalent discretion to exempt the margin lending ban, the short selling ban, or the short-term/speculative trading ban in section 11, or to permit a purchase during a blackout period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC derivative falls outside Securities definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Scentre Group Securities means (collectively) ... any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bespoke, bilateral OTC put/call written by a bank is not 'able to be traded on a financial market', so it falls outside 'Scentre Group Securities' and the general blackout/clearance regime in sections 3-9 does not apply to entering it; only the free-standing 11(d) short-term ban and the statutory Insider Trading Prohibition still apply.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing carved out of margin lending ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities ... they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if structured as a bespoke secured facility rather than a margin loan, is expressly permitted subject only to prior Company Secretary approval, not the outright ban in 11(a).

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lender enforcement excluded from blackout
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank's facility is not a margin loan, its enforcement sale of the collared shares during a blackout period is excluded from the trading restriction, giving a workable enforcement path even in a closed period; this protection would not apply if the facility were characterised as a margin loan for a KMP.

bespoke_clauses.topic: short-term ban reaches OTC derivatives regardless
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because this prohibition names 'Financial Products' rather than 'Scentre Group Securities', it catches the OTC collar even though the collar itself sits outside the Securities definition, so collar tenor should exceed three months and the underlying shares should already be held for 3+ months.

bespoke_clauses.topic: excluded trading list limited to blackout
bespoke_clauses.clause: The following dealings are excluded from the trading restrictions in sections 3 and 4
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The standard carve-outs (trading plans, super fund transfers, rights issues, DRPs, etc.) excuse only blackout-period trading; none of them excuses the section 11 margin lending, short selling or short-term/speculative bans, so the collar cannot rely on these exclusions to escape section 11.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging substance is in an external policy
bespoke_clauses.clause: These prohibitions are outlined in the Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The operative hedging prohibition for unvested and holding-locked/deferred incentive awards is not set out in this document; the bank must obtain and review that separate policy before structuring a collar touching any unvested or locked incentive securities.

summary: A funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted Scentre Group or Carindale securities appears achievable, turning on a definitional feature: a bespoke, bilateral OTC put/call with a bank is not 'able to be traded on a financial market' and so falls outside the 'Scentre Group Securities' definition, meaning the general blackout-period and pre-trade clearance regime does not apply to entering it, although the standalone short-term/speculative trading ban (less than 3 months) and the statutory Insider Trading Prohibition still apply regardless. The loan leg is also workable: section 11 bans only arrangements 'properly described as' margin lending, and expressly permits other secured financing over Scentre Group Securities subject to prior Company Secretary approval, with a lender's enforcement sale under such a facility excluded from the blackout restriction (unless it is a margin loan and the person is Key Management Personnel). Hedging of unvested awards, or vested awards still subject to a holding lock or deferred delivery, is separately and absolutely prohibited under the Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy, an external document not contained in this file and which must be reviewed before proceeding. None of the standard blackout carve-outs (trading plans, rights issues, super transfers) excuses the section 11 restrictions, so those must be independently satisfied. Overall: feasible for vested, unrestricted holdings with Company Secretary approval for the secured facility and a tenor exceeding three months, but the derivative leg's favourable treatment depends on the OTC product genuinely not being tradable on a financial market.
